Follow-up to the W2 catalog expansion (#1608/#1614) and the pushdown audit discipline (#1532). Of the 18 GX types UC currently runs on the pandas frame batch, 14 are pushdown-eligible — GX has SqlAlchemy providers for all of them, proven by the 2026-08-28 live-Snowflake verification (same engine class):

`be_null` · `not_be_in_set` · `value_lengths_to_equal` · `not_match_regex` · `match_regex_list` · `not_match_regex_list` · `pair_values_to_be_equal` · `pair_values_to_be_in_set` · `pair_a_to_be_greater_than_b` · `multicolumn_sum_to_equal` · `select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record` · `distinct_values_to_be_in_set` · `distinct_values_to_contain_set` · `compound_columns_to_be_unique`

**Per-type acceptance (the #1532 bar):** each joins `SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES` only after a live Databricks-SQL run proves payload shape, `unexpected_percent`, and sample-failure extraction. `compound_columns_to_be_unique` additionally needs the #1616 reflection-casing treatment for the Databricks dialect (the shipped fold is Snowflake-runner-scoped) — live-verify the uppercase-column case specifically.

**Explicitly out of scope:** `to_be_of_type`/`in_type_list` (pushdown flips the authored pandas-dtype vocabulary to dialect type strings — breaking, needs its own decision) and `match_strftime_format`/`be_json_parseable` (no SQL provider in GX, `dataframe_only`).

**Why:** frame-batch checks read the whole table into worker memory; pushdown keeps worker memory flat (#1532's original motivation).

**Standing policy (user direction, 2026-08-28):** any NEW check type on Databricks/UC lands as pushdown by default; the frame batch is the exception and needs a recorded reason (no SQL provider, dtype semantics, sampling). Recorded in CLAUDE.md §5 and at the `SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES` declaration.

prove it with `POST /connections/{id}/test` per connection** — the connections list will look
identical whether they are alive or dead.

"""Live-Databricks-SQL verification for #1624 — the 14 newly-pushed-down UC expectation
types, run through the REAL production runner (UnityCatalogCheckRunner.run_checks) against
real dataq_retail tables. Proves: routing (SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES), payload shape,
unexpected_percent correctness (checked against independently-computed ground truth), and
sample-failure extraction. Also proves the compound_columns_to_be_unique uppercase-column
reflection-casing fix is load-bearing (raw GX call without the fold KeyErrors; our runner,
which folds, succeeds).
"""

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ")
os.environ["UC_SQL_PUSHDOWN"] = "true"

from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec
from backend.app.datasources.unity_catalog import UnityCatalogConfig, UnityCatalogCheckRunner

token = os.environ["DBX_TOKEN"]
config = UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(
    {
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
    }
)
runner = UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=config, token=token, catalog="dataq_retail")


def show(label, outcome):
    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")
    for c in outcome.checks:
        print(
            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "
            f"observed={c.observed_value} sample_failures={c.sample_failures}"
        )


# ── Group A: reference.locations (8 rows) ──
show(
    "locations",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="locations",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b",
                {"column_A": "close_hour", "column_B": "open_hour"},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"], "sum_total": 30},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"]},
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

# ── Group B: reference.channels (3 rows) ──
show(
    "channels",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="channels",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set",
                {"column": "channel", "value_set": ["online", "store", "marketplace"]},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_distinct_values_to_contain_set",
                {"column": "channel", "value_set": ["online", "store"]},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_to_be_in_set",
                {
                    "column_A": "channel",
                    "column_B": "is_online",
                    "value_pairs_set": [
                        ["online", True],
                        ["store", False],
                        ["marketplace", True],
                    ],
                },
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

# ── Group C: reference.categories (25 rows) — incl. the #1624 uppercase-column proof ──
show(
    "categories",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="categories",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique", {"column_list": ["CATEGORY_ID"]}
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique",
                {"column_list": ["CATEGORY_ID", "DEPARTMENT"]},
            ),
            CheckSpec("expect_column_value_lengths_to_equal", {"column": "category_id", "value": 8}),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_values_to_not_match_regex",
                {"column": "department", "regex": "^M"},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_values_to_match_regex_list",
                {"column": "department", "regex_list": ["^Mens$", "^Womens$"], "match_on": "any"},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_values_to_not_match_regex_list",
                {"column": "department", "regex_list": ["^Kids$"]},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_values_to_not_be_in_set",
                {"column": "department", "value_set": ["Beauty"]},
            ),
            CheckSpec("expect_column_values_to_be_null", {"column": "category_name"}),
        ],
    ),
)

# ── Group D: reference.date_dim (539 rows) — ground truth 535/539 mismatched ──
show(
    "date_dim",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="date_dim",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_to_be_equal",
                {"column_A": "fiscal_week", "column_B": "fiscal_quarter"},
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

# ── Proof the reflection-casing fold is load-bearing: raw GX WITHOUT the fold KeyErrors ──
print("\n=== raw GX, no fold, uppercase column_list (expect KeyError) ===")
import great_expectations as gx

context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
_, batch_definition = runner._sql_batch_definition(context, table="categories", schema="reference")
try:
    from backend.app.datasources.gx_runner import run_expectations

    outcome = run_expectations(
        context,
        batch_definition=batch_definition,
        checks=[CheckSpec("expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique", {"column_list": ["CATEGORY_ID"]})],
        name="raw-no-fold",
    )
    print("UNEXPECTED: no error.", outcome.checks[0])
except Exception as exc:
    print(f"CONFIRMED trap without the fold: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

runner.close()
print("\nDONE")
